clue.text: Provided money for a fight in deed!

indicators.note: in places the fight inside the word for an act, read as a container signal

parts.note: taken as written, a deed being an act
a fray is a fight or brawl

explanation.surface: An exclamation about someone who actually paid for a fight to take place.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue hangs on 'indeed', which the setter wants read as two words, 'in deed': FRAY goes into DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to pay them, so having defrayed is having supplied the cash for something.

clue.text: Brimstone in store, for a tyrant!

indicators.note: in says the brimstone goes inside the store

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse
brimstone is sulphur, chemical symbol S

explanation.surface: A tyrant keeps sulphur in stock, perhaps for hellfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly.

clue.text: An agitator to sack 'and stigmatise

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
to brand someone is to mark them out with disgrace

explanation.surface: A troublemaker one would like to dismiss and denounce.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is someone who stirs up trouble or rebellion.

clue.text: A strange rite 26 briefly noted?

indicators.note: strange says the letters of rite are oddly arranged

parts.note: the reserve army of 26 across is commonly shortened to its initials

explanation.surface: A puzzled note about an odd ceremony performed by reservists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns RITE into RIET; '26 briefly' is TA, the short form of the Territorial Army; 'noted?' hints at a piece set to musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An arietta is a short aria, a song written out in musical notation.

clue.text: One of two I abandoned' in the upper regions

indicators.note: abandoned says the letter I is left out

parts.note: either means one or the other of two
taken as written

explanation.surface: One of a pair, left alone, up in the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: The ether is the clear sky or upper air, once thought filled with a fine substance.

clue.text: Contract to build extremely swish place for skaters

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the first and last letters, of swish

parts.note: a rink is an ice surface for skating

explanation.surface: A deal to build a smart new ice rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, a building contract, but it is the verb meaning get smaller; 'to build' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to become smaller, the same as to shrink.

clue.text: Hound worrying a cross-country runner

explanation.surface: A dog chasing a cross-country athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrier is a hound bred for hunting hares and harrying them; harriers is also a name for cross-country running clubs.

clue.text: Woman briefly dwelling in state.

parts.note: Ida is a woman's name
ho. is the short form of house, a dwelling

explanation.surface: A woman stays for a short time in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: Ida is the woman; the shortened dwelling is HO, the abbreviation of house.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Need Greek ingredients, not 28, for this dish

indicators.note: ingredients suggests the letters are mixed together as in cooking

parts.note: the answer to 28 across, whose abbreviation is a single letter

explanation.surface: A recipe calling for Greek ingredients, but not from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not 28' takes out N, short for northern, from NEED GREEK; 'ingredients' mixes the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a dish of rice, flaked fish and eggs.

clue.text: . Law-breaker's proposal to admit downfall

definitions.note: with 's read as is, the definition is just the law-breaker

indicators.note: to admit means to let something inside, so the proposal holds the downfall

parts.note: an offer is a proposal
an end is a downfall or demise

explanation.surface: A criminal's plea bargain that concedes his ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is someone who commits a crime.

clue.text: Frank is right ahead

explanation.surface: A claim that being candid is simply correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A frank person is honest and direct; going right ahead is going straight on with no turns.

clue.text: Gold piece a queen presented to a ring-maker

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is a small piece
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: A jeweller's scene: gold presented by a queen to the man who makes rings.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'ring-maker' sounds like a jeweller; here it is something that traces a circular path round a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiter is a spacecraft circling a body, so it traces a loop round it.

clue.text: Digression is found in a lyric poem

indicators.note: found in says the word is sits inside the poem

parts.note: an epode is a kind of lyric poem, as in Horace
taken as written

explanation.surface: A literary note that a lyric poem contains a digression.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode can be an incidental passage or digression within a larger narrative.

clue.text: Made up for being unbiased

explanation.surface: Compensating by being fair-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: To have balanced something is to have offset or compensated for it; a balanced view is impartial.

clue.text: The vessel which is, we are told, referred to in Macbeth

definitions.text: The vessel which is, we are told, referred to in Macbeth

parts.words: The vessel which is, we are told, referred to in Macbeth
parts.note: the witches' pot in Shakespeare's play, plus a sound-alike: the word sounds like a pot named in the play

explanation.surface: A quiz question about a pot mentioned in Shakespeare's Scottish play.
explanation.walkthrough: The witches brew their spells in one in Macbeth; 'we are told' hints the word is also referred to by sound, 'cauld' for cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron is a large cooking pot, famously the witches' vessel in Macbeth.

clue.text: Male dog at first rejected a frill

indicators.note: at first puts the turned dog in front of the male
rejected means the word for dog is thrown back, read backwards

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A male dog spurns a frilly collar at first sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male dog' reads as one phrase, but 'Male' and 'dog' are separate pieces, and 'at first' moves the reversed dog to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a gathered strip of fabric used as trimming, a kind of ruffle.

clue.text: Crowd from Cape going in the right direction

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
on course means heading the right way

explanation.surface: A throng heading from a cape the right way.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a gathering or throng of people.

clue.text: He's more ready to act when we're lost for words

definitions.text: He's more ready to act when we're lost for words

parts.words: He's more ready to act when we're lost for words
parts.note: readable as more ready, the comparative of quick, and as the theatre helper who feeds forgotten lines

explanation.surface: Someone who speaks up readily when others are tongue-tied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more ready to act' is the comparative of prompt; in a theatre this person gives actors their lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompter in the theatre supplies forgotten lines to actors.

clue.text: Part of a Pindar ode on a cattle round-up

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A classical poet's ode about cowboys herding livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo was originally the gathering of herds of livestock on a ranch.

clue.text: Materials in one pail, like hydrated silica

indicators.note: the materials, or raw letters, in the words are rebuilt into a new word

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about substances in a bucket resembling silica.
explanation.walkthrough: Opal is a form of hydrated silica.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline means resembling opal, a gem of hydrated silica.

clue.text: Uranium purchase being applied to promote insurrection

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
purchase is leverage, so applying it is prising something open

explanation.surface: Buying uranium in order to stir up a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying; it is a grip or lever, and using it is prising.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a popular revolt against authority.

clue.text: Garment just one in a suit doesn't have on

indicators.note: doesn't have says the word on is left out

parts.note: a singleton in bridge is the only card held in a suit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garment that is the lone piece of a suit not worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing; it is a card suit, and a singleton is a lone card in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest.

clue.text: It's used by many an artist over there

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
yon is an old word for over there

explanation.surface: Something that many artists use over there.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening words 'It's used by', with everything after supplying the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured stick of wax, this is a drawing tool used by artists.

clue.text: Runs in, angry about everyone getting a duck

indicators.note: in says the runs go inside the rest
about says the angry word surrounds everyone

parts.note: mad means angry
all means everyone
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: an irate batsman scores no runs, getting a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture, runs and a duck, is a trap: the duck is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck.

clue.text: Slow movement of river flowing into Italian lake

indicators.note: flowing into says the river goes inside the lake

parts.note: lago is Italian for lake

explanation.surface: A river flowing slowly into an Italian lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction for a slow, broad tempo, and a movement in that tempo.

clue.text: Deep-seated bitterness of a private soldier, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, not an officer

explanation.surface: The lasting resentment felt by an ordinary soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, which drops the final r, the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is long-held resentment or ill will.

clue.text: Money for one whose skin became wrinkled? Just so

definitions.text: one whose skin became wrinkled? Just so

explanation.surface: Paying an animal with wrinkly skin from Kipling.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kipling's Just So Stories the rhinoceros got his folded skin from cake crumbs; rhino is also old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is dated slang for cash; Kipling's rhinoceros got a folded hide in a Just So story.

clue.text: Leaders of Tommy Atkins's defence force

definitions.text: Leaders of Tommy Atkins's defence force

parts.words: Leaders of Tommy Atkins's defence force
parts.note: the initials of Tommy Atkins, the nickname for a British soldier, are the initials of a British volunteer reserve army

explanation.surface: The commanders of the ordinary British soldier's army.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Atkins is the traditional name for a British private; his initials T A are the familiar abbreviation of this reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve, a home defence force of the army.

clue.text: Lived wantonly, retired, to awfully dire surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the jumbled dire goes round the other piece
awfully says the letters of dire are badly arranged
retired means the word to goes back, read the other way

explanation.surface: Someone who lived a wild life and then retired to dreadful surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like a life stage after wild living; here it only turns a short word backwards, and 'awfully' scrambles DIRE into RIED around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To riot can mean to indulge in dissipated revelry, living without restraint.

clue.text: "But I am constant as the .. star" (J. Caesar)

definitions.text: "But I am constant as the .. star" (J. Caesar)

parts.words: "But I am constant as the .. star" (J. Caesar)
parts.note: fill the gap in Caesar's boast in Shakespeare's play about the fixed pole star

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's Julius Caesar with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar compares his constancy to the pole star, which stays fixed in the sky in the north.
